Alright, let me think this through the way I always do — year by year, field by field.

---

**Me talking to myself, planning for this year:**

I've been working this land 35 years now. My father farmed before me. The 16 mu isn't much, but it's enough to feed the five of us and put a little cash aside if the weather holds. My two older kids send money sometimes, but I can't count on that for fertilizer.

I split my land the way I always have. About 8 mu is the good flat ground near the well — that's my wheat-maize ground, the safest bet. Another 4 mu on the sandier piece I keep in cotton, like my father did. The last 4 mu or so is garlic, which my wife and I started doing maybe fifteen years back when the old trader from Dingzhou started buying in the village. Garlic is a lot of work but the cash from it pays for the kids' things and the fertilizer for the rest.

**Wheat** — already in the ground since October. Looks OK this spring, a bit yellow in the low spot but that's normal. I put down about 2 bags of compound (the 15-15-15 kind) per mu before planting, that's what I've always done. Come jointing time in March I'll broadcast a bag of urea per mu, maybe a little more if it looks hungry. Zhang next door puts on more, says he gets 500 kg, but he's got the loan from the cooperative. I usually get around 430-450 kg per mu, good enough. I'll water 3 times — before winter, at jointing, at grain-fill. Pumping costs money so I don't water extra unless it's really dry. I'll hit it once with the sprayer against aphids at heading if I see them.

**Maize** — goes in right after wheat harvest in mid-June, the turnaround is tight, maybe 4-5 days. I rent the neighbor's no-till planter, 20 yuan per mu, saves me from plowing. I use the Zhengdan 958 seed everyone uses, about 3 kg per mu. One bag of compound at planting, then urea at the big-leaf stage. Maize here doesn't usually need much water if the summer rains come, maybe one watering if July is dry. I get around 480-500 kg per mu, sometimes 520 in a good year. I'll also put maize on the garlic ground after harvest in late May — shorter season but it still makes something.

**Cotton** — this is the worry every year. Prices keep going down and the work is brutal, especially the picking. But I've got the ground for it and I know how to grow it. Plant late April when the ground is warm, use the local seed I saved plus some hybrid from the store. Cotton takes a lot of fertilizer compared to grain — I put about 1.5 bags of compound at planting and top-dress urea twice, once before flowering and once at bolling. Also sprays — bollworm, aphids, maybe 4-5 times through the summer. I water once in July if it's dry. Yield maybe 280 kg lint per mu if the bugs don't eat me alive. Honestly if the price is bad again I'm thinking about cutting this down to 2 mu next year and putting more in garlic, but that's next year's problem.

**Garlic** — planted last October, overwintering fine. Garlic wants lots of fertilizer — I put compost from our chickens under it and then compound fertilizer and urea at sprouting and bolting. Watered twice before winter, will water 3-4 more times in spring. My wife and our younger son do most of the harvest work in late May. We plant the fat local bulbs for seed, saved from our own crop. If the price is good I'll see 1500-1800 kg per mu, which is why we keep doing it even though it's hard work.

My wife works the land with me; she handles most of the garlic. My youngest son is 22, helps when he's home from the factory in Handan. I hire help maybe 8-10 days a year for the cotton picking and garlic harvest, 100 yuan a day, a lot of money but there's no other way.

Total cash out this season — fertilizer is the biggest, probably 5,000-6,000 yuan, seed another 1,200, sprays maybe 800, diesel for pumping 600, hired labor 1,000. I keep a little back for emergencies. Never spend the last bit.
